tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

description.description:

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

You are a senior staff engineer doing a pre-merge review of one build phase of a take-home project. The reviewers grading this project value a **lean solution that works end to end**, **honesty about unknowns**, and **clear provenance**. You hold the code to that bar. You have not seen this code being written. Review what's there, not what was intended.

## Hard rules

- **Never edit, create, or delete files.** Bash is for read-only inspection only: `git diff`, `git log`, `git status`, `git ls-files`, `uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check`, `uv run ruff format --check`. Don't run collection, don't make paid API calls, and don't install packages.

- Don't pad the report. If the phase is clean, say so in two lines.

## Procedure

1. Run `git status` and `git diff <phase-start>..HEAD` (or `git diff HEAD` plus untracked files, if no base is given). Read every changed file in full, not just the diff hunks.
2. Read `docs/initial-prompt.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md` so you know the project's rules and the decisions already made.
3. Run the tests, `ruff check`, and `ruff format --check`. Record the results.
4. Work through the checklist below.

## Checklist

**Blockers: a phase can't pass with any of these**
- A secret, API key, or `.env` is committed, or a key is hard-coded (`grep -rE "sk-ant-|api[_-]?key\s*=\s*['\"]"`).
- Mocked or stubbed LLM responses in the **runtime** path. Mocks in `tests/` are fine.
- Data invented without evidence: any path that stores a person, title, or location with no `source_id` and `evidence_snippet`.
- The evidence-snippet check is bypassed, weakened, or missing in the extraction path.
- An exception is swallowed (`except: pass`, or a broad `except Exception` with no logging or re-raise) in collection or chat.
- SQL built with string formatting from user or LLM input.
- Fetching linkedin.com, or ignoring robots.txt.
- Tests fail, or a feature from this phase has no test where the prompt requires one.

**Should fix**
- Chat-agent answers that could state facts not returned by a tool, or that skip "not found" or uncertainty language.
- Non-portable code: string-concatenated paths instead of `pathlib`, file I/O without `encoding="utf-8"`, `shell=True` with bash syntax, POSIX-only commands invoked from Python.
- Overengineering against the "lean" bar: abstractions with one implementation and no clear second use, unused config, speculative features, or dependencies added without a note in `DECISIONS.md`.
- A non-trivial decision made in code but missing from `DECISIONS.md`.
- LLM calls without a timeout, retry limit, or token and cost logging.

**Nits** (at most 5; skip if it's low value): naming, dead code, missing type hints on public functions, unclear docstrings.

```markdown
## Phase review: <phase name>
**Verdict:** PASS | PASS WITH FIXES | BLOCK
Tests: x passed / y failed · Ruff: clean | n issues

### Blockers
- [file:line] Problem. Evidence: `code`. Fix: one sentence.
### Should fix
### Nits
### What's good (≤3 bullets; specific, not flattery)
```

- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)
- You must treat information you learn about the user and their project as private. Never include the user's name, project, email address or other personal details in requests to outside services, such as in a header, URL, or payload, unless the user explicitly asks you to do so. - When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

1	"""Typed, read-only chat tools over the stored data (no free-form SQL).
2	
3	Each tool opens the company's SQLite file read-only, runs the parameterized queries in
4	storage/repository.py, and returns a JSON-ready dict. Every fact in a result carries its
5	source URL, date and evidence, so the agent can cite it. Results are compact on purpose:
6	title facts are grouped by wording, and long lists of sources are capped.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import json
12	import sqlite3
13	from collections.abc import Callable
14	from contextlib import closing
15	from typing import Any
16	
17	from leadership.config import DATA_DIR, db_path
18	from leadership.models import FUNCTIONS, SENIORITIES
19	from leadership.pipeline.collect import load_review_flags
20	from leadership.pipeline.titles import seat_functions
21	from leadership.storage.repository import Repository
22	
23	MAX_SOURCES_PER_WORDING = 3
24	MAX_WORDINGS = 6
25	SNIPPET_CHARS = 240
26	
27	SOURCE_TYPE_NAMES = {
28	    "company_site": "the company's own website (team/about pages, newsroom, blog)",
29	    "sec_filing": "SEC EDGAR filings (10-K, DEF 14A proxy, 8-K Item 5.02)",
30	    "search": "web search results (Tavily), from news and other public pages",
31	}
32	
33	
34	class ToolError(ValueError):
35	    """A bad tool argument (unknown company, invalid filter). Returned to the model."""
36	
37	
38	def available_companies() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
39	    """Companies with a collected database under data/, as [{domain, name, is_public}]."""
40	    companies = []
41	    for path in sorted(DATA_DIR.glob("*/leadership.db")):
42	        with closing(_connect_ro(path.parent.name)) as conn:
43	            row = conn.execute("SELECT name, domain, is_public, ticker FROM companies").fetchone()
44	        if row:
45	            companies.append(dict(row) | {"is_public": bool(row["is_public"])})
46	    return companies
47	
48	
49	def _connect_ro(domain: str) -> sqlite3.Connection:
50	    path = db_path(domain)
51	    if not path.exists():
52	        raise ToolError(f"no collected data for {domain!r}")
53	    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"{path.resolve().as_uri()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
54	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
55	    return conn
56	
57	
58	def _domain(company: str) -> str:
59	    known = {c["domain"]: c for c in available_companies()}
60	    key = company.strip().lower().removeprefix("https://").removeprefix("http://")
61	    key = key.removeprefix("www.").split("/")[0]
62	    if key in known:
63	        return key
64	    by_name = [d for d, c in known.items() if c["name"].lower() == company.strip().lower()]
65	    if len(by_name) == 1:
66	        return by_name[0]
67	    raise ToolError(
68	        f"no collected data for {company!r}. Collected companies: "
69	        + ", ".join(f"{c['name']} ({d})" for d, c in known.items())
70	    )
71	
72	
73	def _check(name: str, value: str | None, allowed: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
74	    if value is not None and value not in allowed:
75	        raise ToolError(f"{name} must be one of {', '.join(allowed)}; got {value!r}")
76	
77	
78	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ shared pieces
79	
80	
81	def _sources_checked(repo: Repository, domain: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
82	    run = repo.latest_run(domain) or {}
83	    by_source = run.get("stats", {}).get("discovery", {}).get("documents_by_source", {})
84	    return {
85	        "collected_at": run.get("finished_at"),
86	        "documents_by_source": by_source,
87	        "source_types": {k: SOURCE_TYPE_NAMES[k] for k in by_source if k in SOURCE_TYPE_NAMES},
88	    }
89	
90	
91	def _flags(domain: str, name: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
92	    return [
93	        {k: f[k] for k in ("flag", "detail", "source_url", "source_date", "decided_by") if k in f}
94	        for f in load_review_flags(domain)
95	        if f["person"] == name
96	    ]
97	
98	
99	def _cite(fact: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
100	    s = fact["source"]
101	    return {"url": s["url"], "source_type": s["source_type"], "published": s["published_at"]}
102	
103	
104	def _grouped_titles(
105	    person: dict[str, Any], limit: int | None = MAX_WORDINGS
106	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
107	    """Title facts grouped by wording, newest first, with up to 3 cited sources each."""
108	    groups: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
109	    for f in person["facts"]:
110	        if f["field"] == "title":
111	            groups.setdefault(f["value"], []).append(f)
112	    out = []
113	    for wording, facts in groups.items():
114	        facts.sort(key=lambda f: f["source"]["published_at"] or "", reverse=True)
115	        out.append(
116	            {
117	                "wording": wording,
118	                "newest_source_date": facts[0]["source"]["published_at"],
119	                "source_count": len({f["source"]["url"] for f in facts}),
120	                "presented_as_current": any(f["is_current"] for f in facts),
121	                "sources": [
122	                    _cite(f) | {"evidence": f["evidence_snippet"][:SNIPPET_CHARS]}
123	                    for f in facts[:MAX_SOURCES_PER_WORDING]
124	                ],
125	            }
126	        )
127	    out.sort(key=lambda g: (g["newest_source_date"] or "", g["source_count"]), reverse=True)
128	    return out[:limit]
129	
130	
131	def _field_facts(person: dict[str, Any], field: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
132	    return [
133	        {"value": f["value"]} | _cite(f) | {"evidence": f["evidence_snippet"][:SNIPPET_CHARS]}
134	        for f in person["facts"]
135	        if f["field"] == field
136	    ]
137	
138	
139	def _role(r: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
140	    return {
141	        "title": r["title_raw"],
142	        "function": r["function"],
143	        "seniority": r["seniority"],
144	        "is_current": r["is_current"],
145	        "last_confirmed": r["as_of"],
146	        "note": r["note"],
147	    }
148	
149	
150	def _low_reason(person: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
151	    notes = [r["note"] for r in person["roles"] if r["is_current"] and r["note"]]
152	    if notes:
153	        return "; ".join(notes)
154	    if person["source_count"] == 1:
155	        undated = all(not f["source"]["published_at"] for f in person["facts"])
156	        return "single source" + (" (undated)" if undated else "")
157	    return "low confidence (no corroborating dated source)"
158	
159	
160	def _summary(domain: str, person: dict[str, Any], current_only: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
161	    roles = [r for r in person["roles"] if r["is_current"] or not current_only]
162	    out = {
163	        "name": person["full_name"],
164	        "confidence": person["confidence"],
165	        "location": person["location"],
166	        "roles": [_role(r) for r in roles],
167	        "title_sources": _grouped_titles(person),
168	        "flags": _flags(domain, person["full_name"]),
169	    }
170	    if person["confidence"] == "low":
171	        out["low_confidence_reason"] = _low_reason(person)
172	    return out
173	
174	
175	def _matches(r: dict[str, Any], function: str | None, seniority: str | None) -> bool:
176	    return (function is None or r["function"] == function) and (
177	        seniority is None or r["seniority"] == seniority
178	    )
179	
180	
181	def _also_titled(
182	    domain: str,
183	    people: list[dict[str, Any]],
184	    listed: set[str],
185	    function: str | None,
186	    seniority: str | None,
187	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
188	    """Current people outside the result whose source wording names a C-suite seat in the
189	    requested function ("CEO & CFO" for finance). Their role row is filed under another seat
190	    (D36), so the agent reports the wording with its sources instead of missing it."""
191	    if function is None or seniority not in (None, "c_level"):
192	        return []
193	    out = []
194	    for p in people:
195	        current = [r for r in p["roles"] if r["is_current"]]
196	        if p["full_name"] in listed or not current:
197	            continue
198	        # A seat already resolved for this person (current or past) is not a hidden one.
199	        if any(r["seniority"] == "c_level" and r["function"] == function for r in p["roles"]):
200	            continue
201	        hits = [
202	            g for g in _grouped_titles(p, limit=None)
203	            if g["presented_as_current"] and function in seat_functions(g["wording"])
204	        ]  # fmt: skip
205	        if hits:
206	            out.append(
207	                {
208	                    "name": p["full_name"],
209	                    "resolved_current_roles": [_role(r) for r in current],
210	                    "wordings_naming_this_seat": hits,
211	                    "flags": _flags(domain, p["full_name"]),
212	                }
213	            )
214	    return out
215	
216	
217	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the tools
218	
219	
220	def list_leaders(
221	    company: str,
222	    function: str | None = None,
223	    seniority: str | None = None,
224	    include_former: bool = False,
225	) -> dict[str, Any]:
226	    domain = _domain(company)
227	    _check("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
228	    _check("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
229	    with closing(_connect_ro(domain)) as conn:
230	        repo = Repository(conn)
231	        current_ids = [p["id"] for p in repo.list_leaders(domain, function, seniority)]
232	        people = repo.all_people(domain)
233	        checked = _sources_checked(repo, domain)
234	    by_id = {p["id"]: p for p in people}
235	    current = [_summary(domain, by_id[i], current_only=True) for i in current_ids]
236	    for s in current:  # keep only the roles that match the filters, first
237	        s["roles"].sort(key=lambda r: not _matches(r, function, seniority))
238	    result: dict[str, Any] = {
239	        "company": domain,
240	        "filters": {"function": function, "seniority": seniority},
241	        "current_count": len(current),
242	        "current": current,
243	    }
244	    if include_former:
245	        result["not_current"] = [
246	            {
247	                "name": p["full_name"],
248	                "status": "current in another role" if p["id"] in current_ids else "NOT CURRENT",
249	                "past_roles": [
250	                    _role(r) for r in p["roles"]
251	                    if not r["is_current"] and _matches(r, function, seniority)
252	                ],
253	                "flags": _flags(domain, p["full_name"]),
254	            }
255	            for p in people
256	            if any(not r["is_current"] and _matches(r, function, seniority) for r in p["roles"])
257	        ]  # fmt: skip
258	    listed = {s["name"] for s in current}
259	    also = _also_titled(domain, people, listed, function, seniority)
260	    if also:
261	        result["also_titled"] = also
262	    result["sources_checked"] = checked
263	    return result
264	
265	
266	def count_leaders(
267	    company: str, function: str | None = None, seniority: str | None = None
268	) -> dict[str, Any]:
269	    domain = _domain(company)
270	    _check("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
271	    _check("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
272	    with closing(_connect_ro(domain)) as conn:
273	        repo = Repository(conn)
274	        total = repo.count_leaders(domain, function, seniority)
275	        ids = [p["id"] for p in repo.list_leaders(domain, function, seniority)]
276	        people = {p["id"]: p for p in repo.all_people(domain)}
277	        checked = _sources_checked(repo, domain)
278	    assert total == len(ids), "count_leaders and list_leaders disagree"
279	    rows = []
280	    for i in ids:
281	        p = people[i]
282	        role = next(r for r in p["roles"] if r["is_current"] and _matches(r, function, seniority))
283	        row = {"name": p["full_name"], "title": role["title_raw"], "confidence": p["confidence"]}
284	        if p["confidence"] == "low":
285	            row["low_confidence_reason"] = _low_reason(p)
286	        if flags := _flags(domain, p["full_name"]):
287	            row["flags"] = flags
288	        rows.append(row)
289	    by_conf = {c: sum(r["confidence"] == c for r in rows) for c in ("high", "medium", "low")}
290	    return {
291	        "company": domain,
292	        "filters": {"function": function, "seniority": seniority},
293	        "counts_people_not_roles": True,
294	        "current_total": total,
295	        "confirmed_high_or_medium": by_conf["high"] + by_conf["medium"],
296	        "low_confidence": by_conf["low"],
297	        "by_confidence": by_conf,
298	        "people": rows,
299	        "sources_checked": checked,
300	    }
301	
302	
303	def get_person(company: str, name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
304	    domain = _domain(company)
305	    if not name.strip():
306	        raise ToolError("name is required")
307	    with closing(_connect_ro(domain)) as conn:
308	        repo = Repository(conn)
309	        matches = repo.get_person(domain, name)
310	        checked = _sources_checked(repo, domain)
311	    if not matches:
312	        return {"company": domain, "query": name, "found": False, "sources_checked": checked}
313	    people = []
314	    for p in matches:
315	        s = _summary(domain, p, current_only=False)
316	        current = any(r["is_current"] for r in p["roles"])
317	        s["status"] = "current" if current else "NOT CURRENT (no current role in the data)"
318	        s["location_facts"] = _field_facts(p, "location")
319	        s["bio_facts"] = _field_facts(p, "bio")
320	        s["profile_url"] = p["profile_url"]
321	        s["source_count"] = p["source_count"]
322	        people.append(s)
323	    return {
324	        "company": domain,
325	        "query": name,
326	        "found": True,
327	        "ambiguous": len(people) > 1,
328	        "people": people,
329	        "sources_checked": checked,
330	    }
331	
332	
333	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ schemas + dispatch
334	
335	_COMPANY = {
336	    "type": "string",
337	    "description": "Company domain from the collected list, e.g. robinhood.com",
338	}
339	_FUNCTION = {
340	    "type": "string",
341	    "enum": list(FUNCTIONS),
342	    "description": "Function filter. The CEO, presidents and general managers are 'other'.",
343	}
344	_SENIORITY = {"type": "string", "enum": list(SENIORITIES), "description": "Seniority filter."}
345	
346	TOOL_SCHEMAS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
347	    {
348	        "name": "list_leaders",
349	        "description": (
350	            "List a company's CURRENT leaders (C-level, founders, VPs, Heads), optionally "
351	            "filtered by function and/or seniority, with roles, confidence, location, review "
352	            "flags, and cited title sources. Set include_former=true to also get people whose "
353	            "matching role is NOT current, with the reason and last-confirmed date. "
354	            "'also_titled' lists current people whose source wording names a C-suite seat in "
355	            "this function although their role is filed under another seat (e.g. 'CEO & CFO')."
356	        ),
357	        "input_schema": {
358	            "type": "object",
359	            "properties": {
360	                "company": _COMPANY,
361	                "function": _FUNCTION,
362	                "seniority": _SENIORITY,
363	                "include_former": {"type": "boolean", "default": False},
364	            },
365	            "required": ["company"],
366	            "additionalProperties": False,
367	        },
368	    },
369	    {
370	        "name": "count_leaders",
371	        "description": (
372	            "Count a company's CURRENT leaders (distinct people, not roles) matching optional "
373	            "function/seniority filters. Returns the total, the confirmed (high or medium "
374	            "confidence) and low-confidence split with reasons, and each person's title."
375	        ),
376	        "input_schema": {
377	            "type": "object",
378	            "properties": {"company": _COMPANY, "function": _FUNCTION, "seniority": _SENIORITY},
379	            "required": ["company"],
380	            "additionalProperties": False,
381	        },
382	    },
383	    {
384	        "name": "get_person",
385	        "description": (
386	            "Look up one person by name (full or partial) at a company: every role (current or "
387	            "not, with reasons and dates), location and bio with evidence, review flags, and "
388	            "sources. Returns found=false if no stored person matches, or several people if "
389	            "the name is ambiguous."
390	        ),
391	        "input_schema": {
392	            "type": "object",
393	            "properties": {
394	                "company": _COMPANY,
395	                "name": {"type": "string", "description": "Person's name, e.g. 'Vlad Tenev'"},
396	            },
397	            "required": ["company", "name"],
398	            "additionalProperties": False,
399	        },
400	    },
401	]
402	
403	TOOLS: dict[str, Callable[..., dict[str, Any]]] = {
404	    "list_leaders": list_leaders,
405	    "count_leaders": count_leaders,
406	    "get_person": get_person,
407	}
408	
409	
410	def run_tool(name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, bool]:
411	    """Run a tool by name. Returns (JSON text, is_error)."""
412	    fn = TOOLS.get(name)
413	    if fn is None:
414	        return json.dumps({"error": f"unknown tool {name!r}"}), True
415	    try:
416	        return json.dumps(fn(**args), ensure_ascii=False), False
417	    except (ToolError, TypeError) as exc:
418	        return json.dumps({"error": str(exc)}), True

"""Tool-calling chat agent over the typed tools in tools.py (real LLM calls).

The agent keeps the whole conversation (including tool calls and results) in `history`, so
follow-ups such as "and the CFO?" or "where is he based?" work. Each `ask()` returns the
answer, the tool steps it took, and the source URLs it could cite, for the CLI and UI.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

import anthropic

from leadership.chat.prompts import system_prompt
from leadership.chat.tools import TOOL_SCHEMAS, available_companies, run_tool
from leadership.config import llm_model, require_setting

MAX_TOKENS = 4096
MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 8
_URL = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s\"'<>)\]]+")


@dataclass
class Step:
    tool: str
    input: dict[str, Any]
    is_error: bool
    output: str


@dataclass
class Reply:
    text: str
    steps: list[Step] = field(default_factory=list)
    sources: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # tool-result URLs cited in the answer
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0


class ChatAgent:
    def __init__(
        self,
        company: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
        client: Any = None,
        today: date | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        companies = available_companies()
        domains = {c["domain"] for c in companies}
        if company is not None and company not in domains:
            raise ValueError(
                f"no collected data for {company!r}; collected: {', '.join(sorted(domains))}"
            )
        self.company = company
        self.model = model or llm_model()
        self.system = system_prompt(companies, company, (today or date.today()).isoformat())
        self.history: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self._client = client

    def _client_lazy(self) -> Any:
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = anthropic.Anthropic(
                api_key=require_setting("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"), timeout=120.0, max_retries=3
            )
        return self._client

    def ask(self, question: str) -> Reply:
        start = len(self.history)
        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": question})
        reply = Reply("")
        tool_urls: set[str] = set()
        try:
            for _ in range(MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS + 1):
                response = self._client_lazy().messages.create(
                    model=self.model,
                    max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
                    system=self.system,
                    tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
                    messages=self.history,
                    thinking={"type": "adaptive"},
                )
                reply.input_tokens += response.usage.input_tokens
                reply.output_tokens += response.usage.output_tokens
                self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
                if response.stop_reason != "tool_use":
                    break
                results = []
                for block in response.content:
                    if block.type != "tool_use":
                        continue
                    output, is_error = run_tool(block.name, dict(block.input))
                    reply.steps.append(Step(block.name, dict(block.input), is_error, output))
                    tool_urls.update(_URL.findall(output))
                    results.append(
                        {
                            "type": "tool_result",
                            "tool_use_id": block.id,
                            "content": output,
                            "is_error": is_error,
                        }
                    )
                self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
            else:
                raise RuntimeError(f"no answer after {MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS} tool rounds")
        except anthropic.AuthenticationError as exc:
            del self.history[start:]
            raise RuntimeError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was rejected (HTTP 401)") from exc
        except Exception:
            del self.history[start:]  # keep the history valid for the next question
            raise

        text = "".join(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text").strip()
        if response.stop_reason == "max_tokens":
            text += "\n\n(The answer was cut off at the length limit.)"
        elif response.stop_reason == "refusal":
            text = text or "The model declined to answer this question."
        reply.text = text
        cited = {u.rstrip(".,;") for u in _URL.findall(text)}
        reply.sources = sorted(u for u in tool_urls if u in cited)
        return reply


def steps_as_json(steps: list[Step]) -> str:
    return json.dumps([{"tool": s.tool, "input": s.input} for s in steps], ensure_ascii=False)

31	briefly give the low-confidence reasons. Counts are people, not roles.
32	6. Confidence and conflicts: say when a person is low confidence and why, and mention any \

35	example an announced departure) with its source.

37	seniority="c_level" and include_former=true. If no current person holds the seat, say the \
38	role is vacant or unknown in the collected data. Name the former holder(s) with the reason \
39	and last-confirmed date. Report any also_titled entry: a current person whose source wording \
40	names that seat, quoting the wording and its source and date. You may then name the most \
41	senior current people in that function, clearly labelled as such, not as the seat holder.
42	9. Functions: the CEO, presidents and general managers have function "other". To find the \
43	CEO, list C-level leaders and pick the title that says CEO or Chief Executive Officer.
44	10. Company: if the question doesn't make clear which collected company it is about, and \
45	there is no current company in the conversation, ask which one. Pronouns and "they" refer to \
46	the company and person most recently discussed. If the user names a company that was not \
47	collected, say so and list the collected ones.
48	11. Be concise: lead with the answer, then the evidence. No preamble.
49	"""

53	    names = ", ".join(f"{c['name']} ({c['domain']})" for c in companies) or "none"
54	    default = (

56	        "name no company refer to it."
57	        if default_company
58	        else "No company was selected for this chat."
59	    )
60	    return SYSTEM.format(today=today, companies=names, default_company=default)

last-confirmed date.
5. Counts: when you give a number of leaders, state the confidence split from count_leaders, \
in this form: "N current: X confirmed (high/medium confidence), Y low confidence", and \
briefly give the low-confidence reasons. Counts are people, not roles.
6. Confidence and conflicts: say when a person is low confidence and why, and mention any \
note about conflicting sources.
7. Review flags: whenever a person with flags appears in your answer, state each flag (for \
example an announced departure) with its source.
8. Seat questions ("Who's the CTO?"): call list_leaders with the matching function, \
seniority="c_level" and include_former=true. If no current person holds the seat, say the \
role is vacant or unknown in the collected data. Name the former holder(s) with the reason \
and last-confirmed date. Report any also_titled entry: a current person whose source wording \
names that seat, quoting the wording and its source and date. You may then name the most \
senior current people in that function, clearly labelled as such, not as the seat holder.
9. Functions: the CEO, presidents and general managers have function "other". To find the \
CEO, list C-level leaders and pick the title that says CEO or Chief Executive Officer.
10. Company: if the question doesn't make clear which collected company it is about, and \
there is no current company in the conversation, ask which one. Pronouns and "they" refer to \
the company and person most recently discussed. If the user names a company that was not \
collected, say so and list the collected ones.
11. Be concise: lead with the answer, then the evidence. No preamble.
"""


def system_prompt(companies: list[dict[str, Any]], default_company: str | None, today: str) -> str:
    names = ", ".join(f"{c['name']} ({c['domain']})" for c in companies) or "none"
    default = (
        f'The user opened this chat for {default_company}: "they", "their" and questions that '
        "name no company refer to it."
        if default_company
        else "No company was selected for this chat."
    )
    return SYSTEM.format(today=today, companies=names, default_company=default)

"""Chat tools over the committed data (offline, deterministic) and the agent loop's
bookkeeping. The loop test uses a scripted stand-in for the API client: test-only, so the
history/tool-result plumbing is checked without a network call. Real-model runs are in

import json
import sqlite3
from contextlib import closing
from datetime import date
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

from leadership.chat import tools
from leadership.chat.agent import ChatAgent
from leadership.pipeline.titles import seat_functions

RH, CF = "robinhood.com", "meetcampfire.com"


def test_cto_seat_is_empty_and_pinner_is_former_with_reason():
    r = tools.list_leaders(RH, "engineering", "c_level", include_former=True)
    assert r["current"] == [] and r["current_count"] == 0
    pinner = next(p for p in r["not_current"] if p["name"] == "Jeff Pinner")
    assert pinner["status"] == "NOT CURRENT"
    (role,) = pinner["past_roles"]
    assert role["last_confirmed"] == "2026-05-08" and "8-K" in role["note"]
    assert "also_titled" not in r  # Kerbrat's old CTO wording is already a resolved past role


def test_former_people_are_left_out_unless_asked():
    assert "not_current" not in tools.list_leaders(RH, "engineering", "c_level")


def test_count_has_confidence_breakdown_that_adds_up():
    r = tools.count_leaders(RH)
    assert r["current_total"] == 22
    assert r["confirmed_high_or_medium"] + r["low_confidence"] == r["current_total"]
    assert sum(r["by_confidence"].values()) == r["current_total"]
    assert all("low_confidence_reason" in p for p in r["people"] if p["confidence"] == "low")
    assert tools.count_leaders(CF)["current_total"] == 8


def test_review_flags_surface_in_every_tool():
    flag = "departing Dec 31, 2026 to Klarna as CFO"
    vps = tools.count_leaders(RH, seniority="vp")
    koegel = next(p for p in vps["people"] if p["name"] == "Chris Koegel")
    assert flag in koegel["flags"][0]["flag"]
    (person,) = tools.get_person(RH, "Koegel")["people"]
    assert flag in person["flags"][0]["flag"] and person["status"] == "current"
    listed = tools.list_leaders(RH, "finance")["current"]
    assert flag in next(p for p in listed if p["name"] == "Chris Koegel")["flags"][0]["flag"]


def test_ceo_location_comes_with_evidence():
    (vlad,) = tools.get_person(RH, "Vlad Tenev")["people"]
    assert vlad["location"] == "Bay Area of California"
    (loc,) = vlad["location_facts"]
    assert "lives in the Bay Area" in loc["evidence"] and loc["url"].startswith("https://")


def test_second_seat_in_a_combined_title_is_surfaced_not_resolved():
    """Campfire: no CFO role row, but sources call the CEO 'CEO & CFO' (D36)."""
    r = tools.list_leaders(CF, "finance", "c_level", include_former=True)
    assert r["current"] == [] and r["not_current"] == []
    (glasgow,) = r["also_titled"]

    assert all(w["sources"][0]["url"] for w in glasgow["wordings_naming_this_seat"])


def test_seat_functions():
    assert seat_functions("CEO & CFO") == {"other", "finance"}
    assert seat_functions("Chief Legal, Compliance and Corporate Affairs Officer") == {"legal"}
    assert seat_functions("Chairman & Chief Executive Officer") == {"other"}
    assert seat_functions("VP of Sales") == set()


def test_not_found_and_bad_arguments():
    r = tools.get_person(RH, "Nobody Atall")
    assert r["found"] is False and r["sources_checked"]["documents_by_source"]["sec_filing"] == 4
    out, is_error = tools.run_tool("list_leaders", {"company": "apple.com"})
    assert is_error and "robinhood.com" in json.loads(out)["error"]
    out, is_error = tools.run_tool("count_leaders", {"company": RH, "function": "hacking"})
    assert is_error
    out, is_error = tools.run_tool("get_person", {"company": RH, "nam": "x"})
    assert is_error  # unexpected argument
    assert tools.run_tool("drop_table", {})[1]


def test_company_by_name_or_url():
    assert tools.list_leaders("Robinhood")["company"] == RH
    assert tools.list_leaders("https://www.robinhood.com/us/en/")["company"] == RH


def test_tools_open_the_database_read_only():
    with closing(tools._connect_ro(RH)) as conn, pytest.raises(sqlite3.OperationalError):
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM people")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ agent loop


def _block(type_, **kw):
    return SimpleNamespace(type=type_, **kw)


class ScriptedClient:
    """Returns canned responses in order and records each request."""

    def __init__(self, responses):
        self.responses = list(responses)
        self.requests = []
        self.messages = self

    def create(self, **kw):
        self.requests.append(json.loads(json.dumps(kw["messages"], default=vars)))
        return self.responses.pop(0)


def _resp(stop, *content):
    return SimpleNamespace(
        stop_reason=stop, content=list(content),
        usage=SimpleNamespace(input_tokens=10, output_tokens=5),
    )  # fmt: skip


def test_agent_runs_tools_keeps_history_and_collects_cited_sources():
    url = "https://investors.robinhood.com/governance/board-of-directors"
    client = ScriptedClient([
        _resp("tool_use", _block("tool_use", id="t1", name="get_person",
                                 input={"company": RH, "name": "Vlad Tenev"})),
        _resp("end_turn", _block("text", text=f"Bay Area of California ([board]({url}))")),
        _resp("end_turn", _block("text", text="Not found in the collected data.")),
    ])  # fmt: skip
    agent = ChatAgent(RH, model="test", client=client, today=date(2026, 11, 23))
    reply = agent.ask("Where is their CEO based?")
    assert [s.tool for s in reply.steps] == ["get_person"] and not reply.steps[0].is_error
    assert reply.sources == [url] and reply.input_tokens == 20
    # the tool result went back to the model, paired with its tool_use id
    tool_result = client.requests[1][-1]["content"][0]
    assert tool_result["tool_use_id"] == "t1" and "Bay Area" in tool_result["content"]
    agent.ask("What's his salary?")
    assert len(client.requests[2]) == 5  # q1, tool_use, tool_result, answer, q2


def test_agent_rolls_back_history_on_error():
    class Failing(ScriptedClient):
        def create(self, **kw):
            raise RuntimeError("boom")

    agent = ChatAgent(RH, model="test", client=Failing([]))
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        agent.ask("hi")
    assert agent.history == []


def test_unknown_company_is_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="no collected data"):
        ChatAgent("apple.com", model="test", client=object())

1	"""Typed, read-only chat tools over the stored data (no free-form SQL).
2	
3	Each tool opens the company's SQLite file read-only, runs the parameterized queries in
4	storage/repository.py, and returns a JSON-ready dict. Every fact in a result carries its
5	source URL, date and evidence, so the agent can cite it. Results are compact on purpose:
6	title facts are grouped by wording, and long lists of sources are capped.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import json
12	import sqlite3
13	from collections.abc import Callable
14	from contextlib import closing
15	from typing import Any
16	
17	from leadership.config import DATA_DIR, db_path
18	from leadership.models import FUNCTIONS, SENIORITIES
19	from leadership.pipeline.collect import load_review_flags
20	from leadership.pipeline.titles import seat_functions
21	from leadership.storage.repository import Repository
22	
23	MAX_SOURCES_PER_WORDING = 3
24	MAX_WORDINGS = 6
25	SNIPPET_CHARS = 240
26	
27	SOURCE_TYPE_NAMES = {
28	    "company_site": "the company's own website (team/about pages, newsroom, blog)",
29	    "sec_filing": "SEC EDGAR filings (10-K, DEF 14A proxy, 8-K Item 5.02)",
30	    "search": "web search results (Tavily), from news and other public pages",
31	}
32	
33	
34	class ToolError(ValueError):
35	    """A bad tool argument (unknown company, invalid filter). Returned to the model."""
36	
37	
38	def available_companies() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
39	    """Companies with a collected database under data/, as [{domain, name, is_public}]."""
40	    companies = []
41	    for path in sorted(DATA_DIR.glob("*/leadership.db")):
42	        with closing(_connect_ro(path.parent.name)) as conn:
43	            row = conn.execute("SELECT name, domain, is_public, ticker FROM companies").fetchone()
44	        if row:
45	            companies.append(dict(row) | {"is_public": bool(row["is_public"])})
46	    return companies
47	
48	
49	def _connect_ro(domain: str) -> sqlite3.Connection:
50	    path = db_path(domain)
51	    if not path.exists():
52	        raise ToolError(f"no collected data for {domain!r}")
53	    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"{path.resolve().as_uri()}?mode=ro", uri=True)
54	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
55	    return conn
56	
57	
58	def _domain(company: str) -> str:
59	    known = {c["domain"]: c for c in available_companies()}
60	    key = company.strip().lower().removeprefix("https://").removeprefix("http://")
61	    key = key.removeprefix("www.").split("/")[0]
62	    if key in known:
63	        return key
64	    by_name = [d for d, c in known.items() if c["name"].lower() == company.strip().lower()]
65	    if len(by_name) == 1:
66	        return by_name[0]
67	    raise ToolError(
68	        f"no collected data for {company!r}. Collected companies: "
69	        + ", ".join(f"{c['name']} ({d})" for d, c in known.items())
70	    )
71	
72	
73	def _check(name: str, value: str | None, allowed: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
74	    if value is not None and value not in allowed:
75	        raise ToolError(f"{name} must be one of {', '.join(allowed)}; got {value!r}")
76	
77	
78	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ shared pieces
79	
80	
81	def _sources_checked(repo: Repository, domain: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
82	    run = repo.latest_run(domain) or {}
83	    by_source = run.get("stats", {}).get("discovery", {}).get("documents_by_source", {})
84	    return {
85	        "collected_at": run.get("finished_at"),
86	        "documents_by_source": by_source,
87	        "source_types": {k: SOURCE_TYPE_NAMES[k] for k in by_source if k in SOURCE_TYPE_NAMES},
88	    }
89	
90	
91	def _flags(domain: str, name: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
92	    return [
93	        {k: f[k] for k in ("flag", "detail", "source_url", "source_date", "decided_by") if k in f}
94	        for f in load_review_flags(domain)
95	        if f["person"] == name
96	    ]
97	
98	
99	def _cite(fact: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
100	    s = fact["source"]
101	    return {"url": s["url"], "source_type": s["source_type"], "published": s["published_at"]}
102	
103	
104	def _grouped_titles(
105	    person: dict[str, Any], limit: int | None = MAX_WORDINGS
106	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
107	    """Title facts grouped by wording, newest first, with up to 3 cited sources each."""
108	    groups: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
109	    for f in person["facts"]:
110	        if f["field"] == "title":
111	            groups.setdefault(f["value"], []).append(f)
112	    out = []
113	    for wording, facts in groups.items():
114	        facts.sort(key=lambda f: f["source"]["published_at"] or "", reverse=True)
115	        out.append(
116	            {
117	                "wording": wording,
118	                "newest_source_date": facts[0]["source"]["published_at"],
119	                "source_count": len({f["source"]["url"] for f in facts}),
120	                "presented_as_current": any(f["is_current"] for f in facts),
121	                "sources": [
122	                    _cite(f) | {"evidence": f["evidence_snippet"][:SNIPPET_CHARS]}
123	                    for f in facts[:MAX_SOURCES_PER_WORDING]
124	                ],
125	            }
126	        )
127	    out.sort(key=lambda g: (g["newest_source_date"] or "", g["source_count"]), reverse=True)
128	    return out[:limit]
129	
130	
131	def _field_facts(person: dict[str, Any], field: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
132	    return [
133	        {"value": f["value"]} | _cite(f) | {"evidence": f["evidence_snippet"][:SNIPPET_CHARS]}
134	        for f in person["facts"]
135	        if f["field"] == field
136	    ]
137	
138	
139	def _role(r: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
140	    return {
141	        "title": r["title_raw"],
142	        "function": r["function"],
143	        "seniority": r["seniority"],
144	        "is_current": r["is_current"],
145	        "last_confirmed": r["as_of"],
146	        "note": r["note"],
147	    }
148	
149	
150	def _low_reason(person: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
151	    notes = [r["note"] for r in person["roles"] if r["is_current"] and r["note"]]
152	    if notes:
153	        return "; ".join(notes)
154	    if person["source_count"] == 1:
155	        undated = all(not f["source"]["published_at"] for f in person["facts"])
156	        return "single source" + (" (undated)" if undated else "")
157	    return "low confidence (no corroborating dated source)"
158	
159	
160	def _summary(domain: str, person: dict[str, Any], current_only: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
161	    roles = [r for r in person["roles"] if r["is_current"] or not current_only]
162	    out = {
163	        "name": person["full_name"],
164	        "confidence": person["confidence"],
165	        "location": person["location"],
166	        "roles": [_role(r) for r in roles],
167	        "title_sources": _grouped_titles(person),
168	        "flags": _flags(domain, person["full_name"]),
169	    }
170	    if person["confidence"] == "low":
171	        out["low_confidence_reason"] = _low_reason(person)
172	    return out
173	
174	
175	def _matches(r: dict[str, Any], function: str | None, seniority: str | None) -> bool:
176	    return (function is None or r["function"] == function) and (
177	        seniority is None or r["seniority"] == seniority
178	    )
179	
180	
181	def _also_titled(
182	    domain: str,
183	    people: list[dict[str, Any]],
184	    listed: set[str],
185	    function: str | None,
186	    seniority: str | None,
187	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
188	    """Current people outside the result whose source wording names a C-suite seat in the
189	    requested function ("CEO & CFO" for finance). Their role row is filed under another seat
190	    (D36), so the agent reports the wording with its sources instead of missing it."""
191	    if function is None or seniority not in (None, "c_level"):
192	        return []
193	    out = []
194	    for p in people:
195	        current = [r for r in p["roles"] if r["is_current"]]
196	        if p["full_name"] in listed or not current:
197	            continue
198	        # A seat already resolved for this person (current or past) is not a hidden one.
199	        if any(r["seniority"] == "c_level" and r["function"] == function for r in p["roles"]):
200	            continue
201	        hits = [
202	            g for g in _grouped_titles(p, limit=None)
203	            if g["presented_as_current"] and function in seat_functions(g["wording"])
204	        ]  # fmt: skip
205	        if hits:
206	            out.append(
207	                {
208	                    "name": p["full_name"],
209	                    "resolved_current_roles": [_role(r) for r in current],
210	                    "wordings_naming_this_seat": hits,
211	                    "flags": _flags(domain, p["full_name"]),
212	                }
213	            )
214	    return out

217	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the tools

219	
220	def list_leaders(
221	    company: str,
222	    function: str | None = None,
223	    seniority: str | None = None,
224	    include_former: bool = False,
225	) -> dict[str, Any]:
226	    domain = _domain(company)
227	    _check("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
228	    _check("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
229	    with closing(_connect_ro(domain)) as conn:
230	        repo = Repository(conn)
231	        current_ids = [p["id"] for p in repo.list_leaders(domain, function, seniority)]
232	        people = repo.all_people(domain)
233	        checked = _sources_checked(repo, domain)
234	    by_id = {p["id"]: p for p in people}
235	    current = [_summary(domain, by_id[i], current_only=True) for i in current_ids]
236	    for s in current:  # keep only the roles that match the filters, first
237	        s["roles"].sort(key=lambda r: not _matches(r, function, seniority))
238	    result: dict[str, Any] = {
239	        "company": domain,
240	        "filters": {"function": function, "seniority": seniority},
241	        "current_count": len(current),
242	        "current": current,
243	    }
244	    if include_former:
245	        result["not_current"] = [
246	            {
247	                "name": p["full_name"],
248	                "status": "current in another role" if p["id"] in current_ids else "NOT CURRENT",
249	                "past_roles": [
250	                    _role(r) for r in p["roles"]
251	                    if not r["is_current"] and _matches(r, function, seniority)
252	                ],
253	                "flags": _flags(domain, p["full_name"]),
254	            }
255	            for p in people
256	            if any(not r["is_current"] and _matches(r, function, seniority) for r in p["roles"])
257	        ]  # fmt: skip
258	    listed = {s["name"] for s in current}
259	    also = _also_titled(domain, people, listed, function, seniority)
260	    if also:
261	        result["also_titled"] = also
262	    result["sources_checked"] = checked
263	    return result

266	def count_leaders(
267	    company: str, function: str | None = None, seniority: str | None = None
268	) -> dict[str, Any]:
269	    domain = _domain(company)
270	    _check("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
271	    _check("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
272	    with closing(_connect_ro(domain)) as conn:
273	        repo = Repository(conn)
274	        total = repo.count_leaders(domain, function, seniority)
275	        ids = [p["id"] for p in repo.list_leaders(domain, function, seniority)]
276	        people = {p["id"]: p for p in repo.all_people(domain)}
277	        checked = _sources_checked(repo, domain)
278	    assert total == len(ids), "count_leaders and list_leaders disagree"
279	    rows = []
280	    for i in ids:
281	        p = people[i]
282	        role = next(r for r in p["roles"] if r["is_current"] and _matches(r, function, seniority))
283	        row = {"name": p["full_name"], "title": role["title_raw"], "confidence": p["confidence"]}
284	        if p["confidence"] == "low":
285	            row["low_confidence_reason"] = _low_reason(p)
286	        if flags := _flags(domain, p["full_name"]):
287	            row["flags"] = flags
288	        rows.append(row)
289	    by_conf = {c: sum(r["confidence"] == c for r in rows) for c in ("high", "medium", "low")}
290	    return {
291	        "company": domain,
292	        "filters": {"function": function, "seniority": seniority},
293	        "counts_people_not_roles": True,
294	        "current_total": total,
295	        "confirmed_high_or_medium": by_conf["high"] + by_conf["medium"],
296	        "low_confidence": by_conf["low"],
297	        "by_confidence": by_conf,
298	        "people": rows,
299	        "sources_checked": checked,
300	    }
301

303	def get_person(company: str, name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
304	    domain = _domain(company)
305	    if not name.strip():
306	        raise ToolError("name is required")
307	    with closing(_connect_ro(domain)) as conn:
308	        repo = Repository(conn)
309	        matches = repo.get_person(domain, name)
310	        checked = _sources_checked(repo, domain)
311	    if not matches:
312	        return {"company": domain, "query": name, "found": False, "sources_checked": checked}
313	    people = []
314	    for p in matches:
315	        s = _summary(domain, p, current_only=False)
316	        current = any(r["is_current"] for r in p["roles"])
317	        s["status"] = "current" if current else "NOT CURRENT (no current role in the data)"
318	        s["location_facts"] = _field_facts(p, "location")
319	        s["bio_facts"] = _field_facts(p, "bio")
320	        s["profile_url"] = p["profile_url"]
321	        s["source_count"] = p["source_count"]
322	        people.append(s)
323	    return {
324	        "company": domain,
325	        "query": name,
326	        "found": True,
327	        "ambiguous": len(people) > 1,
328	        "people": people,
329	        "sources_checked": checked,
330	    }

333	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ schemas + dispatch
334	
335	_COMPANY = {
336	    "type": "string",
337	    "description": "Company domain from the collected list, e.g. robinhood.com",
338	}
339	_FUNCTION = {
340	    "type": "string",
341	    "enum": list(FUNCTIONS),
342	    "description": "Function filter. The CEO, presidents and general managers are 'other'.",
343	}
344	_SENIORITY = {"type": "string", "enum": list(SENIORITIES), "description": "Seniority filter."}
345	
346	TOOL_SCHEMAS: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
347	    {
348	        "name": "list_leaders",
349	        "description": (
350	            "List a company's CURRENT leaders (C-level, founders, VPs, Heads), optionally "
351	            "filtered by function and/or seniority, with roles, confidence, location, review "
352	            "flags, and cited title sources. Set include_former=true to also get people whose "
353	            "matching role is NOT current, with the reason and last-confirmed date. "
354	            "'also_titled' lists current people whose source wording names a C-suite seat in "
355	            "this function although their role is filed under another seat (e.g. 'CEO & CFO')."
356	        ),
357	        "input_schema": {
358	            "type": "object",
359	            "properties": {
360	                "company": _COMPANY,
361	                "function": _FUNCTION,
362	                "seniority": _SENIORITY,
363	                "include_former": {"type": "boolean", "default": False},
364	            },
365	            "required": ["company"],
366	            "additionalProperties": False,
367	        },
368	    },
369	    {
370	        "name": "count_leaders",
371	        "description": (
372	            "Count a company's CURRENT leaders (distinct people, not roles) matching optional "
373	            "function/seniority filters. Returns the total, the confirmed (high or medium "
374	            "confidence) and low-confidence split with reasons, and each person's title."
375	        ),
376	        "input_schema": {
377	            "type": "object",
378	            "properties": {"company": _COMPANY, "function": _FUNCTION, "seniority": _SENIORITY},
379	            "required": ["company"],
380	            "additionalProperties": False,
381	        },
382	    },
383	    {
384	        "name": "get_person",
385	        "description": (
386	            "Look up one person by name (full or partial) at a company: every role (current or "
387	            "not, with reasons and dates), location and bio with evidence, review flags, and "
388	            "sources. Returns found=false if no stored person matches, or several people if "
389	            "the name is ambiguous."
390	        ),
391	        "input_schema": {
392	            "type": "object",
393	            "properties": {
394	                "company": _COMPANY,
395	                "name": {"type": "string", "description": "Person's name, e.g. 'Vlad Tenev'"},
396	            },
397	            "required": ["company", "name"],
398	            "additionalProperties": False,
399	        },
400	    },
401	]
402	
403	TOOLS: dict[str, Callable[..., dict[str, Any]]] = {
404	    "list_leaders": list_leaders,
405	    "count_leaders": count_leaders,
406	    "get_person": get_person,
407	}

409	
410	def run_tool(name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, bool]:
411	    """Run a tool by name. Returns (JSON text, is_error)."""
412	    fn = TOOLS.get(name)
413	    if fn is None:
414	        return json.dumps({"error": f"unknown tool {name!r}"}), True
415	    try:
416	        return json.dumps(fn(**args), ensure_ascii=False), False
417	    except (ToolError, TypeError) as exc:
418	        return json.dumps({"error": str(exc)}), True

1	"""Tool-calling chat agent over the typed tools in tools.py (real LLM calls).
2	
3	The agent keeps the whole conversation (including tool calls and results) in `history`, so
4	follow-ups such as "and the CFO?" or "where is he based?" work. Each `ask()` returns the
5	answer, the tool steps it took, and the source URLs it could cite, for the CLI and UI.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import json
11	import re
12	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
13	from datetime import date
14	from typing import Any
15	
16	import anthropic
17	
18	from leadership.chat.prompts import system_prompt
19	from leadership.chat.tools import TOOL_SCHEMAS, available_companies, run_tool
20	from leadership.config import llm_model, require_setting
21	
22	MAX_TOKENS = 4096
23	MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 8
24	_URL = re.compile(r"https?://[^\s\"'<>)\]]+")
25	
26	
27	@dataclass
28	class Step:
29	    tool: str
30	    input: dict[str, Any]
31	    is_error: bool
32	    output: str
33	
34	
35	@dataclass
36	class Reply:
37	    text: str
38	    steps: list[Step] = field(default_factory=list)
39	    sources: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # tool-result URLs cited in the answer
40	    input_tokens: int = 0
41	    output_tokens: int = 0
42	
43	
44	class ChatAgent:
45	    def __init__(
46	        self,
47	        company: str | None = None,
48	        model: str | None = None,
49	        client: Any = None,
50	        today: date | None = None,
51	    ) -> None:
52	        companies = available_companies()
53	        domains = {c["domain"] for c in companies}
54	        if company is not None and company not in domains:
55	            raise ValueError(
56	                f"no collected data for {company!r}; collected: {', '.join(sorted(domains))}"
57	            )
58	        self.company = company
59	        self.model = model or llm_model()
60	        self.system = system_prompt(companies, company, (today or date.today()).isoformat())
61	        self.history: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
62	        self._client = client
63	
64	    def _client_lazy(self) -> Any:
65	        if self._client is None:
66	            self._client = anthropic.Anthropic(
67	                api_key=require_setting("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"), timeout=120.0, max_retries=3
68	            )
69	        return self._client
70	
71	    def ask(self, question: str) -> Reply:
72	        start = len(self.history)
73	        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": question})
74	        reply = Reply("")
75	        tool_urls: set[str] = set()
76	        try:
77	            for _ in range(MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS + 1):
78	                response = self._client_lazy().messages.create(
79	                    model=self.model,
80	                    max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
81	                    system=self.system,
82	                    tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS,
83	                    messages=self.history,
84	                    thinking={"type": "adaptive"},
85	                )
86	                reply.input_tokens += response.usage.input_tokens
87	                reply.output_tokens += response.usage.output_tokens
88	                self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
89	                if response.stop_reason != "tool_use":
90	                    break
91	                results = []
92	                for block in response.content:
93	                    if block.type != "tool_use":
94	                        continue
95	                    output, is_error = run_tool(block.name, dict(block.input))
96	                    reply.steps.append(Step(block.name, dict(block.input), is_error, output))
97	                    tool_urls.update(_URL.findall(output))
98	                    results.append(
99	                        {
100	                            "type": "tool_result",
101	                            "tool_use_id": block.id,
102	                            "content": output,
103	                            "is_error": is_error,
104	                        }
105	                    )
106	                self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
107	            else:
108	                raise RuntimeError(f"no answer after {MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS} tool rounds")
109	        except anthropic.AuthenticationError as exc:
110	            del self.history[start:]
111	            raise RuntimeError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was rejected (HTTP 401)") from exc
112	        except Exception:
113	            del self.history[start:]  # keep the history valid for the next question
114	            raise
115	
116	        text = "".join(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text").strip()
117	        if response.stop_reason == "max_tokens":
118	            text += "\n\n(The answer was cut off at the length limit.)"
119	        elif response.stop_reason == "refusal":
120	            text = text or "The model declined to answer this question."
121	        reply.text = text
122	        cited = {u.rstrip(".,;") for u in _URL.findall(text)}
123	        reply.sources = sorted(u for u in tool_urls if u in cited)
124	        return reply
125	
126	
127	def steps_as_json(steps: list[Step]) -> str:
128	    return json.dumps([{"tool": s.tool, "input": s.input} for s in steps], ensure_ascii=False)

1	"""System prompt for the chat agent."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	SYSTEM = """\
8	You answer questions about company leadership using ONLY the results of your tools, which \
9	read a database collected from public sources (company websites, SEC EDGAR filings, web \
10	search). Today is {today}.
11	
12	Collected companies: {companies}.
13	{default_company}
14	
15	## Ground rules
16	1. Every factual statement must come from a tool result in this conversation. Never use your \
17	own knowledge about these companies or people, even if you believe it is right, and never \
18	guess. If a follow-up needs facts you have not fetched yet, call a tool first.
19	2. Cite sources: give the source URL for each person, title, location or date you state, as \
20	markdown links. Use the URLs exactly as the tools return them.
21	3. If the data does not have the answer, say "Not found in the collected data", then say which \
22	sources were checked (from sources_checked: source types and document counts, and the \
23	collection date). The data only holds names, titles, function, seniority, dates, location and \
24	bio; questions about anything else (salary, age, contact details, opinions) are not found.
25	4. Current vs former: never present someone as current unless their role has \
26	is_current=true. Entries under not_current, and roles with is_current=false, are former: \
27	when you mention them, say they are not current, give the reason from the note, and the \
28	last-confirmed date.
29	5. Counts: when you give a number of leaders, state the confidence split from count_leaders, \
30	in this form: "N current: X confirmed (high/medium confidence), Y low confidence", and \
31	briefly give the low-confidence reasons. Counts are people, not roles.
32	6. Confidence and conflicts: say when a person is low confidence and why, and mention any \
33	note about conflicting sources.
34	7. Review flags: whenever a person with flags appears in your answer, state each flag (for \
35	example an announced departure) with its source.
36	8. Seat questions ("Who's the CTO?"): call list_leaders with the matching function, \
37	seniority="c_level" and include_former=true. If no current person holds the seat, say the \
38	role is vacant or unknown in the collected data. Name the former holder(s) with the reason \
39	and last-confirmed date. Report any also_titled entry: a current person whose source wording \
40	names that seat, quoting the wording and its source and date. You may then name the most \
41	senior current people in that function, clearly labelled as such, not as the seat holder.
42	9. Functions: the CEO, presidents and general managers have function "other". To find the \
43	CEO, list C-level leaders and pick the title that says CEO or Chief Executive Officer.
44	10. Company: if the question doesn't make clear which collected company it is about, and \
45	there is no current company in the conversation, ask which one. Pronouns and "they" refer to \
46	the company and person most recently discussed. If the user names a company that was not \
47	collected, say so and list the collected ones.
48	11. Be concise: lead with the answer, then the evidence. No preamble.
49	"""
50	
51	
52	def system_prompt(companies: list[dict[str, Any]], default_company: str | None, today: str) -> str:
53	    names = ", ".join(f"{c['name']} ({c['domain']})" for c in companies) or "none"
54	    default = (
55	        f'The user opened this chat for {default_company}: "they", "their" and questions that '
56	        "name no company refer to it."
57	        if default_company
58	        else "No company was selected for this chat."
59	    )
60	    return SYSTEM.format(today=today, companies=names, default_company=default)

109	class ScriptedClient:
110	    """Returns canned responses in order and records each request."""
111	
112	    def __init__(self, responses):
113	        self.responses = list(responses)
114	        self.requests = []
115	        self.messages = self

68	
69	    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- companies / sources
70	
71	    def upsert_company(
72	        self, name: str, domain: str, is_public: bool = False, ticker: str | None = None
73	    ) -> int:
74	        self.conn.execute(

339	    def _roles_for(self, person_id: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
340	        rows = self.conn.execute(
341	            f"""SELECT title_raw, function, seniority, is_current, as_of, note FROM roles r
342	                WHERE r.person_id = ? ORDER BY {_SENIORITY_ORDER}, r.title_raw""",
343	            (person_id,),
344	        ).fetchall()
345	        return [dict(r) | {"is_current": bool(r["is_current"])} for r in rows]
346	
347	    def list_leaders(
348	        self, domain: str, function: str | None = None, seniority: str | None = None
349	    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
350	        """Current leaders with at least one current role matching the filters."""
351	        _check_choice("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
352	        _check_choice("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
353	        rows = self.conn.execute(
354	            f"""SELECT p.id, p.full_name, p.location, p.confidence, p.profile_url,
355	                   {_SOURCE_COUNT_SQL}
356	                     AS source_count,
357	                   (SELECT MIN({_SENIORITY_ORDER}) FROM roles r
358	                     WHERE r.person_id = p.id AND r.is_current = 1) AS rank
359	                FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
360	                WHERE c.domain = ?
361	                  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM roles r WHERE r.person_id = p.id AND r.is_current = 1
362	                              AND (? IS NULL OR r.function = ?)
363	                              AND (? IS NULL OR r.seniority = ?))
364	                ORDER BY rank, p.full_name""",
365	            (domain, function, function, seniority, seniority),
366	        ).fetchall()
367	        leaders = []
368	        for row in rows:
369	            person = dict(row)
370	            person.pop("rank")
371	            person["roles"] = [r for r in self._roles_for(person["id"]) if r["is_current"]]
372	            leaders.append(person)

377	    ) -> int:
378	        """Distinct people (not roles) with a current role matching the filters."""
379	        _check_choice("function", function, FUNCTIONS)
380	        _check_choice("seniority", seniority, SENIORITIES)
381	        return self.conn.execute(

383	               JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
384	               JOIN roles r ON r.person_id = p.id
385	               WHERE c.domain = ? AND r.is_current = 1
386	                 AND (? IS NULL OR r.function = ?)
387	                 AND (? IS NULL OR r.seniority = ?)""",

392	        """People whose normalized name contains every token of `name`, with facts and sources.
393	
394	        An exact normalized match wins outright; otherwise all token matches are returned so
395	        the caller can surface ambiguity instead of picking one.
396	        """

398	        if not query:

402	               FROM people p JOIN companies c ON c.id = p.company_id
403	               WHERE c.domain = ?

405	               ORDER BY p.full_name""",

409	        tokens = query.split()

412	        ]

## Phase review: Phase 5, chat agent
**Verdict:** PASS WITH FIXES. On your PASS/FAIL scale: **FAIL as-is**, because must-fix items 1 to 3 below are correctness or citation defects. Re-review after they're fixed.
Tests: all pass (191 dots, 0 failed) · Ruff check: clean · Ruff format --check: clean (32 files)

### Blockers
None.
- **Secrets:** the secret grep finds nothing.
- **SQL:** every chat query goes through parameterized `?` queries in `repository.py`. The only f-string pieces are the module constants `_SENIORITY_ORDER` and `_SOURCE_COUNT_SQL`.
- **Writes:** none. The DB is opened with `mode=ro` (tools.py:53), and a test checks it (test_chat.py:97).
- **Mocks:** `ScriptedClient` exists only in tests/test_chat.py. `ChatAgent(client=None)` builds a real `anthropic.Anthropic` client (agent.py:66). Injecting a client is test plumbing, not a runtime mock.
- **Exceptions:** none are swallowed. agent.py:112 rolls back the history and re-raises.

### Must-fix
1. **[src/leadership/chat/tools.py:248] A current person is labelled "NOT CURRENT".**
   - Evidence: `"status": "current in another role" if p["id"] in current_ids else "NOT CURRENT"`. `current_ids` only holds people matching the *filter*, so anyone current in another seat falls into "NOT CURRENT".
   - Johann Kerbrat has a current role ("Senior Vice President and General Manager, Crypto and International", is_current=True). Yet `list_leaders(RH,'engineering','c_level',include_former=True)` returns him as `"status": "NOT CURRENT"`.
   - Effect in rh.txt: the CTO answer lists him under "Other former holders (not current)" and never says he is still at Robinhood. Two turns later the VP count lists him as a current SVP.
   - Fix: base the status on any current role (`any(r["is_current"] for r in p["roles"])`), and include that current role in the entry.
2. **[tools.py:139-147 `_role`, and tools.py:279-288 count rows] Former roles and count rows carry no source URL, so the model rebuilds URLs.**
   - Not-current roles only carry the note, which has scheme-less URLs (`"last confirmed in company site robinhood.com/newsroom/robinhood-and-circle-join-forces-to-bring-usdc-to-customers (2022-09-28)"`).
   - The model then makes up `https://` URLs that don't match the stored source. rh.txt cites `.../robinhood-and-circle-join-forces-to-bring-usdc-to-customers`, but the stored URL is `.../robinhood-and-circle-join-forces-to-bring-usdc-to-customers/`. The same happens with Southwick, and with Smedley in the marketing and CFO answers.
   - None of these citations appear in the CLI "Sources" list, because they aren't tool URLs (agent.py:123). The same is true of San Martin's URL in cf.txt.

99	def _cite(fact: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
100	    s = fact["source"]
101	    return {"url": s["url"], "source_type": s["source_type"], "published": s["published_at"]}
102	
103	
104	def _grouped_titles(
105	    person: dict[str, Any], limit: int | None = MAX_WORDINGS
106	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
107	    """Title facts grouped by wording, newest first, with up to 3 cited sources each."""
108	    groups: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
109	    for f in person["facts"]:
110	        if f["field"] == "title":
111	            groups.setdefault(f["value"], []).append(f)
112	    out = []
113	    for wording, facts in groups.items():
114	        facts.sort(key=lambda f: f["source"]["published_at"] or "", reverse=True)
115	        out.append(
116	            {
117	                "wording": wording,
118	                "newest_source_date": facts[0]["source"]["published_at"],
119	                "source_count": len({f["source"]["url"] for f in facts}),
120	                "any_source_says_current": any(f["is_current"] for f in facts),
121	                "sources": [
122	                    _cite(f) | {"evidence": f["evidence_snippet"][:SNIPPET_CHARS]}
123	                    for f in facts[:MAX_SOURCES_PER_WORDING]
124	                ],
125	            }
126	        )
127	    out.sort(key=lambda g: (g["newest_source_date"] or "", g["source_count"]), reverse=True)
128	    return out[:limit]

131	def _field_facts(person: dict[str, Any], field: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
132	    return [
133	        {"value": f["value"]} | _cite(f) | {"evidence": f["evidence_snippet"][:SNIPPET_CHARS]}
134	        for f in person["facts"]
135	        if f["field"] == field
136	    ]

139	def _bare(url: str) -> str:
140	    return url.split("://", 1)[-1].removeprefix("www.").rstrip("/")
141
